rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=param_efficient-claude-agentic iter-11 SIX-BOX (FIX the iter-10 learned-init WIRING BUG). PREV RESULT iter-10 (learned-init refiner): hr 0, ssim 0.2923, psnr 11.38, RMSE 0.01349 (18x iter-7's 0.00074), 2010p. FROZE: epoch-1 train loss 1.9e-4 = exactly 100x iter-7's epoch-1 (3.4e-6), then flat 8 epochs, alpha barely moved, output degenerate. CHAMPION iter-7 (foe nf24/k7/nb31, 1921p, K=5 tied prox+DC, scalar alpha, 16-ep cosine) hr 0.2515 ssim 0.906 psnr 36.59. FAILURE MODE (a WIRING BUG, NOT a science result): the iter-10 head was correctly zero-init (g(.)=0 at init), BUT forward CLAMPED the raw LD-FBP to [0,clip_max] BEFORE the unroll: x_0=clamp(LD-FBP+g(LD-FBP),0,clip_max). clip_max==display_max==0.05; the LD-FBP has bright pixels (bone/contrast/spine mu>0.05) and iter-7 NEVER clamps its init (starts x=u0 RAW). So the init clamp TRUNCATED the LD-FBP -> x_0 was NOT byte-for-byte iter-7 (numerically verified: ||x0-u0||/||u0||=6.8e-2 from the clamp alone) -> unroll started from a corrupted high-RMSE init (100x epoch-1 loss) and never recovered. The learned-init HYPOTHESIS was never tested, only a broken build. CHANGE (CODE, +177 params, K=5 KEPT): re-wire the learned-init CORRECTLY. (1) TRUE byte-for-byte init: x_0=u0+g(u0) with NO upper clamp (clamp_min(0) only, a no-op since LD-FBP>=0); the unroll's per-step clamp handles range, exactly like iter-7's x=u0. So at init (g=0) x_0==LD-FBP EXACTLY. (2) SMOOTH refiner (avoids the dead-ReLU-before-zero-head trap): conv(1->16,3x3)->GELU->conv(16->1,1x1) with BOTH the 1x1 head weight AND bias zero-init (verified nn.init.zeros_ on each). 16*9+16 + 16+1 = 177p; total=1921+177=2098p (<233k ITNet). (3) RUNTIME SELF-CHECK (the guard iter-10 lacked): right after building the model, on one val sample, print rel=||g(LD_FBP)||/||LD_FBP|| AND ||x0-LD_FBP||/||LD_FBP|| and ASSERT both <1e-6, so a non-zero-init / init-clamp bug FAILS LOUDLY before the 20-min run is wasted. Numerically verified on cluster: rel_g=0.000e+00, rel_x0=0.000e+00 (PASS). UNROLL byte-for-byte iter-7: reg_type=foe nf24/k7/nb31 (1920p zero-init rho), n_iter=5, single scalar alpha, NO momentum/per-step alpha, plain prox, cosine 5e-3->1e-5, 16 ep, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, bs=1, val_n=214. STABILITY (STAYS in the iter-7 basin, unlike iter-8/9/10): (1) TRUE zero-init AND no init clamp => x_0==LD-FBP byte-for-byte, the self-check ENFORCES it; (2) K STAYS 5 (iter-9's K=7 diverged) -- g is OUTSIDE the loop, applied once; (3) FoE bank STAYS 1920p (iter-8's nf=40 diverged); (4) g single-scale, NO pooling (iter-2/5 failure), eff RF ~3px, a local refiner not a denoiser; (5) +1 cheap conv pass/forward, dominated by the 5 DC project pairs, so 16-ep cosine still fits the 1331s iter-7 wall under the 1080s backstop. HYPOTHESIS: a TRULY zero-init refiner gives epoch-1 train loss == iter-7's (~3e-6, NOT 1e-4); refining x_0 with a tiny zero-init learned filter lowers the RMSE the K=5 contraction starts from -> lower final RMSE (the headroom gate) -> hr ABOVE 0.2515 at +177p, SAME K=5/1921p-unroll. A MATCH ~0.25 maps init-saturation (the unroll drives the init to its fixed point regardless of x_0 -- a clean frontier result iter-10 could not measure); a REGRESSION means the refiner learned a destructive correction despite zero-init (diagnosable, revert). PREDICTED hr ~0.25-0.30., reg_type=foe, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, per_step_alpha=False, momentum=False, cnn_channels=12, cnn_layers=3, alpha_init=0.1, clip_max=0.05, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, cosine_lr_min=1e-05, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, foe_rbf_init_std=0.0, foe_filter_init_std=0.05, foe_x_range=1.0, learned_init=True, init_channels=16, init_layers=1, init_clamp=False

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=iter-10 SIX-BOX (NEW ARCHITECTURE STAGE: learned-init refiner of the LD-FBP). PREV CHAMPION iter-7 (foe nf24/k7/nb31, 1921p, K=5 tied prox+DC, scalar alpha, 16-ep cosine) hr 0.2515 ssim 0.906 psnr 36.59. DEAD LEVERS: iter-8 SCALED the FoE bank nf24->40 and TOTALLY DIVERGED (psnr 1.87); iter-9 DEEPENED the unroll K5->7 and DIVERGED (psnr 11.38). Both capacity AND depth blow up in 20 min: iter-7 is a SHARP, NARROW stable optimum (K=5, 1921p, 16-ep). FAILURE MODE: with reg-capacity and unroll-depth both exhausted, attack the part that is NEITHER: the INITIALISATION. iter-7 starts the unroll from the raw LD-FBP (psnr ~34.08 floor); the headroom GATE is RMSE-vs-LD-FBP and the unroll is a contraction, so a LOWER-RMSE x_0 maps to a LOWER final RMSE. CHANGE (CODE, +89 params, K=5 KEPT, a real two-stage architecture not a config tweak): ADD a tiny ZERO-INIT learned-init refiner g applied ONCE to the LD-FBP before the unroll: x_0 = clamp(LD-FBP + g(LD-FBP), 0, clip_max). g = 1->8 3x3 conv, ReLU, zero-init 1x1 head (init_channels=8, init_layers=1 => 8*9+8 + 8+1 = 89p). Total = 1921 + 89 = 2010p (<2.2k, <233k ITNet). UNROLL UNCHANGED iter-7 byte-for-byte: reg_type=foe nf24/k7/nb31 (1920p zero-init rho), n_iter=5, single scalar alpha, NO momentum/per-step alpha, plain prox, cosine 5e-3->1e-5, 16 ep, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, bs=1, val_n=214. STABILITY (why it STAYS in the iter-7 basin, unlike iter-8/9): (1) ZERO-INIT head => g=0 at init so x_0==LD-FBP EXACTLY, the seed IS iter-7 byte-for-byte; training only learns a correction (same zero-init-output pattern as CNNReg head / FoE rho). (2) K STAYS 5 -- the unroll dynamics iter-9 destabilised are UNTOUCHED; g is OUTSIDE the loop, applied once, so it cannot interact with the per-step alpha that over-stepped at K=7. rationale: manhart_pwls_tv-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=iter-5 manhart_pwls_tv LAST TV-tuning probe. CONTEXT: gamma is a CONFIRMED-INERT lever (data term ~1000x below TV term at tv_lambda=0.001 -> iter-1 g=1.0 and iter-2 g=0.5 bit-identical hr=0.13349 to 17 digits); dropping tv_lambda 0.001->1e-4 (iter-4) to activate gamma COLLAPSED hr 0.2071->0.0592 (under-regularized/noisy). So Manhart statistical ray-weighting adds nothing on dense full-view Mayo; the solver is pinned to plain-TV behaviour. iter-3 hr-best 0.2071 (tv_clip_max=0.08, gamma=1.0 inert, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=200, tv_lr=0.01) sits just BELOW plain-TV peak hr=0.2085. tv_clip_max is the ONLY confirmed-wired lever that moved the needle (0.05->0.08 drove hr 0.1335->0.2071). This probes ONE knob: tv_clip_max 0.08->0.10 (the documented upper bound of the (0.05,0.10) TV search range, monotone-improvement direction, NO extra iterations so same ~1533s compute, fits 20-min budget). HYPOTHESIS: a slightly looser TV clip lets manhart edge to ~0.21 and just past plain-TVs 0.2085; if it does not exceed 0.2085 this CONFIRMS manhart pinned at the plain-TV ceiling and the solver is a closed negative. ONE knob; all else = iter-3 base., tv_clip_max=0.1

rationale: manduca_bilateral-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=six-box manduca_bilateral iter-4 (EXPLORATORY). (a) PRIOR FLAT: iter-1 (proj_sr=1.5) hr=0.05982; iter-2 (proj_sr=3.0) hr=0.05978; iter-3 (bf_d_w_ratio 1/6->0.5 i.e. proj spatial sigma 0.83px->2.5px, AND proj range wide) hr=0.05983. So EVERY proj-domain bilateral lever (range bandwidth proj_sr, spatial footprint bf_d_w_ratio) is FLAT to <1e-4. (b) FAILURE MODE / WHY PROJ-BILATERAL IS FLAT: the truncation-corrected FBP is already a strong reconstruction; the ~7-param proj-domain bilateral acts on the SINOGRAM before backprojection, where its tiny correction is smeared across all detector channels and largely washed out by the ramp filter + backprojection averaging, contributing almost nothing to the final image-domain SSIM/headroom. The binding constraint is NOT projection-domain noise bandwidth - it is that no operator is yet touching the reconstructed IMAGE where SSIM/hr are actually measured (img_n_bf=1 is a single shallow image-bilateral pass). (c) LEVER (one knob): img_n_bf 1->2, stacking a second image-domain trainable bilateral filter directly on the reconstructed image. This is a genuinely DIFFERENT axis from the 3 flat proj-domain iters: it doubles the image-domain denoising capacity at the exact location where the calibrated-SSIM-headroom metric lives, so surviving soft-tissue noise in the FBP output gets a second edge-preserving smoothing pass - the most direct route to move SSIM/hr. (d) BUDGET: +1 image-bilateral filter is ~7 extra params and one extra cheap conv per forward pass -> wall stays ~387-563s as iter-1/2/3, comfortably inside the hard 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=3 (hr-best @ 0.05983, marginally best; preserves the iter-3 proj spatial-sigma=2.5px state and layers the image-domain capacity on top)., bf_d_w_ratio=0.5, img_n_bf=2

rationale: manhart_pwls_tv-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=iter-3 PIVOT after gamma-inert diagnosis. iter-1(g=1.0) and iter-2(g=0.5) gave BIT-IDENTICAL hr=0.13349368501203374/ssim=0.9267/psnr=35.32 to 17 digits. Slurm logs (769099/769168) PROVE gamma reached the recon: W differs (min 0.0001 vs 0.0107, max 3.131 vs 2.367) and data_term differs (0.01696 vs 0.04011). NOT a key-mismatch, NOT unwired. rationale: manduca_bilateral-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=six-box manduca_bilateral iter-3 (EXPLORATORY). (a) PRIOR: iter-1 (proj_sr=1.5) hr=0.05982; iter-2 (proj_sr=3.0) hr=0.05978 -> proj_sr FLAT (range bandwidth NOT the binding constraint over 1.5-3.0). (b) FAILURE MODE: the proj-bilateral spatial footprint is sub-pixel. With proj_w=5 and bf_d_w_ratio=1/6, proj spatial sigma = (1/6)*5 = 0.83 px < 1 px, so the kernel averages essentially only the center detector sample. No matter how wide the RANGE kernel (proj_sr) is opened, there are no spatial neighbors being pooled, so soft-tissue noise survives into the FBP and hr is pinned. The range bandwidth can only bite once the spatial reach covers real neighbors. (c) LEVER (one knob): bf_d_w_ratio 1/6(=0.167) -> 0.5, raising proj spatial sigma 0.83px -> 2.5px (a genuine ~5-tap pooling footprint), which finally lets the already-wide range kernel average surviving mid-Q soft-tissue noise -> higher calibrated-SSIM-headroom. This is the paper-locked d/w degree of freedom, the highest-impact lever given the tiny (~7-param) capacity where kernel geometry IS the denoising strength. (d) BUDGET: no capacity/epoch change -> ~387-557s wall as in iter-1/2, well inside the 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=1 (hr-best; iter-2 is tied within noise)., bf_d_w_ratio=0.5

With N0=1e5, Q in [0,~316] and the sqrt/Anscombe noise std ~0.5 sqrt-counts; proj_sr=1.5 only averages pixels within +/-1.5 sqrt-counts so the dominant mid-Q soft-tissue noise (where Mayo SSIM is gated) survives into the FBP. (c) Lever: proj_sr 1.5 -> 3.0 (one knob) widens the range kernel to ~6 noise-sigma so the proj-bilateral averages more surviving soft-tissue noise, raising calibrated-SSIM-headroom. (d) No capacity/epoch change -> same ~387s wall, well inside 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=1., proj_sr=3.0
